summary: Intermittent 429s for large upload callbacks when Content-Encoding + chunked transfer present
description:
Issue summary:
Customer DataStride reports intermittent 429 responses for callback requests following large multipart embedding uploads. Problem only observed when client uploads use Content-Encoding: gzip together with chunked Transfer-Encoding and the signed callback URL contains query parameters.

Impact:
- Affects background ingestion callbacks from DataStride to Redwood: callbacks being rejected with 429 cause their retry loop to back off and delay ingestion completion (estimated 10-20% of callbacks during peak).
- Customer is on Dedicated tier; they see quota depletion on the route-level counters while tenant-level quota appears healthy.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (dedicated-2-uswest), prod-us-west region
- Requests use customer-signed callback URLs (signed query params) that include callback_id and timestamp
- Transfers are chunked with Content-Encoding: gzip on the request body

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Initiate large multipart embedding upload (>50MB) using the SDK; SDK does chunked upload with gzip encoding.
2) Redwood issues callback to signed URL with query params after finalization.
3) Callback sometimes receives 429 from our gateway.

Expected behavior:
- Callback should be accepted (2xx) unless tenant or route quota is exhausted. Route-level accounting should reflect callback token usage mapped to the tenant key and not double-count due to request normalization.

Observed behavior:
- Gateway returns 429 for the callback. Console shows route-level token window reaching limit within seconds for callbacks only; tenant bucket remains under threshold.

Initial customer-provided headers (sanitized):
- Content-Encoding: gzip
- Transfer-Encoding: chunked
- Host: callback.datastride.example
- Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
- X-Forwarded-For: 34.122.11.5

Attached artifacts from customer: request trace IDs (cust-trace-1001..1006), sample signed callback URL (redacted), and SDK version (datastride-sdk/2.7.1).
steps_to_reproduce: (Copy of customer steps) 1) Upload large payload via SDK using gzip+chunked 2) Wait for Redwood callback 3) Observe 429s intermittently for callbacks 10-20% of time
logs: Edge logs show 429 responses for inbound callback path /callback/receive?cid=... with reason code RATE_ROUTE_EXHAUST (rn:route-203). Token accounting trace: route-window: consumed=1000, tenant-window: consumed=1200/5000. Timestamp cluster: 2026-03-10T18:12:xxZ. Proxy layer normalized URL (edge-proxy) by stripping trailing empty query parameters and reordering query string which appears to map callback to a different route fingerprint in the route-layer meter. See excerpt: "normalized_path=/callback/receive?callback_id=abc&ts=161&sig=..." then later counted as /callback/receive?sig=...&ts=161&callback_id=abc
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-10 19:00 Support triage (Maya): validated customer traces and verified reproduced behavior with internal SDK emulator.
- 2026-03-10 20:10 SRE (Luis) pulled edge-proxy normalization debug logs for those traces and found query string reordering during header-inspection pass.
- 2026-03-10 21:30 Hypothesis: when Content-Encoding: gzip + chunked is present, the edge proxy performs a fast-path header normalization that canonicalizes query params for downstream routing; the route-layer uses a fingerprint that includes the canonicalized query string leading to inconsistent mapping between initial signed URL (used during route setup) and perceived route when measuring quota. This causes the route-meter to attribute callbacks to a transient route-fingerprint with a very small ephemeral quota, exhausting it quickly and returning 429 even though tenant-level tokens are available.
- Corroborating evidence: reproducer run with curl (no chunked + no gz) had no 429s. Reproducer using chunked+gzip triggered rapid route-window depletion.
- Edge-proxy code paths flagged: request_normalize_query() in edge-proxy v1.9.3; route-meter fingerprinting in rate-limiter service expects normalized_path to match signed-url fingerprint created at issuance.

Open questions:
- Is canonicalization deterministic but different between signer code and edge-proxy?
- Does route-meter use entire query string or only whitelisted params?
comments: 2026-03-10 19:05 Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Collected customer traces and asked for SDK logs and signed callback sample. Notified SRE on-call.
2026-03-10 20:22 Luis Gomez (SRE): Pulled proxy traces. Early sign of query param reordering in the normalization step. Scheduling deeper trace capture on next reproduction window.

2026-03-11 09:14 DataStride (customer): We can temporarily disable gzip encoding on callbacks side if it helps with triage. Their SDK can toggle content-encoding but chunking is part of their upload flow (hard to change immediately).

2026-03-11 12:01 Luis Gomez (SRE): Confirmed reproduction in a staging dedicated pool. Created internal INT ticket to track code change: INT-4412. Temporary mitigation: set an ingress rule to skip query normalization for paths matching /callback/receive for this customer (requires config push).
2026-03-11 13:30 Maya Chen (Support): Applied config bypass on staging and customer reports callbacks accepted in test run. Scheduling prod change with change freeze window outside business hours.
2026-03-12 02:10 Luis Gomez (SRE): Hotfix deployed to prod: edge-proxy skip-normalize for /callback/receive for DataStride (config id cfg-psk-772). Monitoring token consumption and callbacks for 24h.
2026-03-12 11:45 DataStride (customer): Reports callback success rate back up to 99% during morning ingestion run. Thanks!
root_cause: Edge proxy query-string canonicalization path normalized signed callback URLs differently than the signer/runtime fingerprinting logic when Content-Encoding: gzip + chunked set, causing route-layer to attribute callbacks to a transient/incorrect route fingerprint with a small ephemeral quota leading to 429s.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: configuration-based bypass of query normalization for /callback/receive on the customer's dedicated ingress; customer-side workaround: option to avoid gzip encoding for callbacks was offered but not required after fix.
Long-term fix: engineering to align signer fingerprinting and edge-proxy normalization logic so route-meter uses canonicalized keys consistent with signer or alternatively switch route-fingerprinting to ignore non-essential query param ordering/signature-preserving canonicalization. INT-4412 tracks implementation plan.
Post-deploy: monitoring dashboard updated to show route-fingerprint drift metric and alert when tenant vs route accounting diverges by >10%.
follow_up_tasks: INT-4412 - Edge-proxy: make query normalization deterministic w/ signer (owner: infra-runtime)
ENG-omega-2026-09 - extend rate-meter to whitelist canonical query params relevant for routing (owner: rate-limiter team)
Update runbook: add step to check normalized_path fingerprint when investigating route-only 429s
